title: Complex Inference Chains
tagline: Year 4 — Chaining if-then statements, contrapositives, only-if and either-or to find what must be true

introduction.overview: A complex inference question gives several linked conditional statements and one or two facts, and asks what must follow. The tools are chaining (if p then q, if q then r gives if p then r), the contrapositive (not q gives not p), the reading of "only if" and "if and only if", and elimination in either-or statements. Because each combination of true and false values is a possible world, a conclusion must be true in every world consistent with the statements.
introduction.placementRelevance: Chained inference items appear in the advanced logical and verbal sections of company tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Reading policies and contracts ("if X then Y") and deciding what follows is the same reasoning.

learningObjectives: Translate "only if" and "if and only if"

requiredTopics: Assumptions, Inferences, and Courses of Action
prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: "If p then q" is equivalent to "if not q then not p", but not to "if q then p". "p only if q" means "if p then q".

coreDefinitions: Chain: if p then q and if q then r give if p then r.
Contrapositive: if not q then not p.
Converse: if q then p (not equivalent).
Only if: p only if q means if p then q.
If and only if: p and q are both true or both false.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A conditional is a one-way street. You may travel forward from cause to effect, and you may reason backwards only by denying the effect.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write each statement as an arrow. Follow arrows forward from known true facts and backwards from known false facts.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Chain
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: p → q, q → r ⇒ p → r

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Only if
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: p only if q ⇒ p → q

mainNarrative: If the project is approved the budget is released; if the budget is released hiring begins; hiring has not begun. Going backwards: no hiring means the budget was not released (contrapositive of the second statement), which means the project was not approved (contrapositive of the first).

Meena did not pass the aptitude test. An interview needs a pass, so she did not get an interview; an offer needs an interview, so no offer. We cannot conclude anything about whether someone who passed gets an offer.
Exactly one plan is adopted; if Plan A then the road is widened; the road is not widened. So Plan A is not adopted, and therefore Plan B is.
The shop is open if and only if the manager is present; if the manager is present the alarm is off; the alarm is on. So the manager is not present, hence the shop is not open.
Either the printer is faulty or the cable is loose; if the cable is loose the signal drops; the signal does not drop. So the cable is not loose, and the printer is faulty.

deepDiveAspects.title: Denying the antecedent
deepDiveAspects.content: From "if p then q" and "not p" you cannot conclude "not q"; q may be true for other reasons.

deepDiveAspects.title: Checking by worlds
deepDiveAspects.content: With three yes-no facts there are only eight worlds; if you are unsure, list those that fit the statements.

solvedExamples.title: Contrapositive
solvedExamples.question: If the project is approved the budget is released; the budget was not released. What follows?

solvedExamples.title: Invalid reversal
solvedExamples.question: If it rains the match is cancelled. The match was cancelled. Did it rain?

solvedExamples.title: Either-or
solvedExamples.question: Either the printer is faulty or the cable is loose. The cable is not loose. What follows?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write arrows, go forward from truths and backward from falsehoods; if unsure, list the worlds that fit.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Translate p only if q to p → q.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options that reverse an arrow.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Valid conclusions follow in every possible world.

easy.question:
Statements: If the project is approved, the budget is released. If the budget is released, hiring begins. Hiring has not begun.

Which of the following must be true?
easy.explanation: Checking every possible situation that fits the statements, "The project was not approved." is true in all of them. Each of the other options is false in at least one situation that fits the statements.

easy.question:
Statements: If the project is approved, the budget is released. If the budget is released, hiring begins. Hiring has not begun.

Which of the following conclusions is valid?
options: Either the project was approved or the budget was released.
easy.explanation: Checking every possible situation that fits the statements, "The budget was not released." is true in all of them. Each of the other options is false in at least one situation that fits the statements.

easy.question:
Statements: If the project is approved, the budget is released. If the budget is released, hiring begins. Hiring has not begun.

Which of the following can be deduced from the statements?
options: Either the project was approved or the budget was released.
easy.explanation: Checking every possible situation that fits the statements, "The project was not approved." is true in all of them. Each of the other options is false in at least one situation that fits the statements.

intermediate.question:
Statements: A candidate gets an interview only if the candidate passes the aptitude test. A candidate gets an offer only if the candidate gets an interview. Meena did not pass the aptitude test.

Which of the following can be deduced from the statements?
options: Meena did not get an offer.
Meena either got an interview or an offer.
intermediate.correctAnswer: Meena did not get an offer.
intermediate.explanation: Checking every possible situation that fits the statements, "Meena did not get an offer." is true in all of them. Each of the other options is false in at least one situation that fits the statements.

advanced.question:
Statements: The shop is open if and only if the manager is present. If the manager is present, the alarm is off. The alarm is on.

Which of the following can be deduced from the statements?
options: The shop is open or the manager is present.
advanced.explanation: Checking every possible situation that fits the statements, "The manager is not present." is true in all of them. Each of the other options is false in at least one situation that fits the statements.
